Q: What SQL function would I use to locate specific words in a dataset? A:

Novice approach

If you want to search a word or a phrase from a RDBMS (Relational Database Management System) using SQL, the novice approach is to search the column with a matching pattern like so:

SELECT *
FROM table_name
WHERE column_name LIKE '%word%'

A word of advice. Don't do that. There are 2 major reasons.

  1. The '%word%' pattern only guarantees that the word appears somewhere in the value of that column. It does not guarantee it's a whole word. So, a '%cat%' pattern not only matches 'cat' but also 'educate', 'certification', etc. That's probably not what you want to match.
  2. The leading '%' wildcard will make the search a non-SARGable one, which means it greatly hurts the performance.

Performance concern

Most database maintainers set up indexes on table columns to improve search performance and make JOIN operations much faster. Indexes are essentially B+ trees, and they increase search speed by several orders of magnitude. But when a wild card '%' appears in the beginning of a pattern, it would force the DB engine to scan the data one by one instead of leveraging the indexes.

  • 'word' or 'word%' would perform index seek, very fast.
  • '%word' would perform index scan, much slower.
  • '%word%' would perform table scan, the slowest possible way.

Not only this would impact your search speed, on an RDBMS shared by multiple users (which is the case in most environments), the database engine would slow down while serving your query, and other users would be affected as well.

Prefer to use a full-text search

Most modern RDBMS support full-text search feature. There are several benefits:

  1. It supports searches on word boundaries: CONTAINS((column_name), 'cat')
  2. It allows a pattern: CONTAINS((column_name), '"cat*"'. When full-text wildcard * is used, the search phrase needs to be quoted with "..." inside the string.
  3. You can use AND / OR / NOT logical operator in the search phrase, eg: CONTAINS((column_name), 'cat OR dog').
  4. When comparing the column_name LIKE '%cat%', the performance is greatly improved.

Different RDBMS would have different set up procedures and different ways to use full-text searches. For Microsoft SQL Server, here are the on-line resource you can look up:

  • Overview: Full-Text Search - SQL Server| Microsoft Learn
  • Create & manage indexes: Create and Manage Full-Text Indexes - SQL Server | Microsoft Learn
  • Getting started: Getting Started with Full-Text Search - SQL Server | Microsoft Learn

PostgreSQL on-line doc:

  • PostgreSQL: Documentation: 18: Chapter 12. Full Text Search
